short_title: distances to a circle from an eccentric diameter point
enunciation: If on the diameter of a circle a point be taken which is not the center of the circle, and from the point segments fall upon the circle, that will be greatest on which the center is, the remainder of the same diameter will be least, and of the rest the nearer to the segment through the center is always greater than the more remote, and only two equal segments will fall from the point on the circle, one on each side of the least segment.

subslides.chapter: / F A / > / F B / > / F C / > / F G / by I.20 and I.24
subslides.symbolic: / F A / > / F B / > / F C / > / F G /
subslides.clause_html:
/ F A / = / E B / + / E F / > / F B /;
< B E F ) > < C E F ) → / F B / > / F C / > / F G /.
subslides.just_title: By triangle inequality (I.20), / F A / > / F B /; by the Hinge Theorem (I.24), greater central angles subtend greater bases.

subslides.chapter: / F G / + / E F / > / E G / = / E D / implies / F G / > / F D /
subslides.symbolic: / F G / + / E F / > / E D / → / F G / > / F D /
subslides.clause_html:
In < G E F >, / F G / + / E F / > / E G / = / E D /
→ subtracting / E F / leaves / F G / > / F D / (least).
subslides.just_title: Two sides / F G / + / E F / exceed the third side / E G / = / E D /; subtracting / E F / leaves / F G / > / F D /.

subslides.chapter: < G E F > ≃ < H E F > → / F G / = / F H /; third equal / F K / impossible
subslides.symbolic: < G E F > ≃ < H E F > → / F G / = / F H /; / F K / = / F G / ⇒⇐
subslides.clause_html:
By SAS, < G E F > ≃ < H E F > → / F G / = / F H /;
if / F K / = / F G /, then / F K / = / F H / (nearer = remote) ⇒⇐
subslides.just_title: SAS congruence (I.4) gives / F G / = / F H /; any third equal line / F K / would violate strict monotonicity.

subslides.just_title: From an eccentric diameter point F, / F A / is greatest, / F D / is least, nearer exceeds remote, and equal pairs are unique.
